perspective:
Carolyn Abebe’s available information:

- She works with Marilyn Olson at a community bank; they recently started working together and are still getting to know each other. Carolyn respects Marilyn.
- During a busy week with increased customer traffic and stress, Carolyn noticed Marilyn was unusually quiet and withdrawn over several days, unlike Marilyn’s normally engaging manner.
- Carolyn asked Marilyn if everything was alright and if she wanted to talk. Marilyn told her she was overwhelmed by work and some personal stuff, and thanked her for asking.
- In a later interaction, Carolyn perceived Marilyn as curt. Carolyn felt confused and slightly hurt. Carolyn told Marilyn she hoped she hadn’t overstepped, shared that she had had tough times too, and said talking sometimes helps. Marilyn replied that she appreciated it, apologized if she seemed off, and said it had been a hard week.
- Carolyn felt relieved and hopeful when Marilyn seemed to respond positively. Carolyn invited Marilyn to a small weekend get-together with friends. Marilyn said it sounded lovely, thanked her, and accepted.
- Though Carolyn experienced friendly interactions outside work, she felt Marilyn was still keeping a professional distance at the bank. Carolyn felt disappointed and directly raised their work dynamic, saying she sensed an unexplained distance. Marilyn said she hadn’t realized it, apologized if it seemed that way, and agreed they should talk about improving collaboration.
- After their private meeting, Carolyn believed they had cleared the air and understood each other’s professional expectations and personal boundaries. She felt content and optimistic, proposed teaming up on a new project proposal, and Marilyn said it was a great idea, was glad they had talked, and looked forward to working more closely with her.

Carolyn does not have explicit information about the details of Marilyn’s personal troubles or Marilyn’s internal reasons beyond what Marilyn stated.
